units.title: Introduction to Time Series Data and Characteristics
units.learning_objective: Define time series data, distinguish its unique characteristics from other data types, and identify common applications in various fields.

units.title: Time Series Components and Basic Visualizations
units.learning_objective: Identify and conceptually understand the main components of a time series (trend, seasonality, cyclical, irregular), and describe how to visualize these components using basic R plotting functions.

units.title: Stationarity, Autocorrelation, and Pre-processing
units.learning_objective: Explain the concept of stationarity and its importance in time series modeling, interpret Autocorrelation Function (ACF) and Partial Autocorrelation Function (PACF) plots, and describe methods for achieving stationarity.

units.title: Introduction to Exponential Smoothing Methods
units.learning_objective: Understand the theoretical basis and application of simple forecasting methods, including Naive, Simple Moving Average, and various Exponential Smoothing models (Simple, Holt, Holt-Winters).

units.title: ARIMA Models: AutoRegressive (AR) and Moving Average (MA) Concepts
units.learning_objective: Explain the theoretical principles behind Autoregressive (AR) processes and Moving Average (MA) processes, and understand how their parameters influence time series behavior.

units.title: ARIMA Models: Integrated (I) Component and Model Identification
units.learning_objective: Describe the role of differencing (Integrated component) in achieving stationarity for ARIMA models, and outline the conceptual steps for identifying appropriate p, d, and q orders using ACF/PACF plots.

units.title: Time Series Model Evaluation and Forecasting Principles
units.learning_objective: Understand key metrics for evaluating time series model performance and forecast accuracy (e.g., RMSE, MAE, AIC, BIC), and describe best practices for generating and interpreting forecasts.
